newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Standard Chartered hikes lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Standard Chartered hikes lending rate.

text.p: One of Zimbabwe's largest commercial banks, Standard Chartered, raised its minimum lending rate by 0.5 percentage points to 29 percent on Monday, citing as a reason recent hikes in statutory reserves by the central Reserve Bank.
"Standard Chartered Bank announces its minimum lending rate will increase by 0.5 percent from 28.5 percent to 29 percent, with effect from December 13, 1996," it said in a statement.

The increase comes barely two months after Standard Chartered Bank and other local banks lowered their minimum lending rate to 28.5 percent from 30 percent on the back of an easing in annual inflation and falling money market rates.
"The announcement of the latest change in Standard Chartered's lending rate follows recent increases in the statutory reserve which banks are required to keep with the Reserve Bank," it added.
Two weeks ago, the Reserve Bank raised to 20 percent from 17.5 percent the statutory reserves banks are required to keep with it.
It said the measure was aimed at curbing money supply growth, which had remained stubbornly above a 22-percent per annum target under economic reforms started in 1991.
Money market dealers and analysts said they expected lending rates to rise as a result of the move.

On Monday, Standard Chartered said the Reserve Bank measure was crucial to control money supply growth, which it said, if left unchecked, was likely to undermine efforts to bring down annual inflation. Annual inflation was pegged at 20.2 percent in October.

But it said that while the increase in the statutory reserve requirements had decreased the amount of money in circulation, a large amount of money had been drawn out of banks at no interest, reducing the amount available for investing or lending to customers and increasing the cost of that lending.
"In the current economic climate, lending rates can be expected to rise or fall as changes in the marketplace dictate," he said.
